title: The Forgotten Thorn
premise: Ada Almeida has spent twenty years as gatekeeper of Hollowgate, the one pass through the Thornfell mountains, keeping his head down and his ledgers clean while smugglers and refugees slip past him for a price. When prayers whispered at his gate begin to be answered by the old gods—gods everyone believed dead—he learns that a child's soul was sold generations ago to the court beneath the mountain to seal an old bargain, and that the usurper King Vessar means to claim that bargain's power for himself. Ada, whose own sister was the soul sold, must gather a found family of smugglers, exiles, and a disgraced priestess to descend beneath Thornfell and steal her back before Vessar's armies reach the free cities. In the end Ada reopens the gate not for coin but for everyone, binding the old gods to the living world and choosing belonging over invisibility.
about_author: Noor Reyes is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write about borders, bargains, and the people who live in between.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Sins
chapters.summary: Ada Almeida's POV. A routine night at Hollowgate: bribes logged, a smuggler waved through, a refugee family turned away with quiet shame. Establishes Ada's careful invisibility and his moral compromises. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Heard
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. An old woman prays at the gatepost—and something answers. Frost blooms out of season; a voice like wind through stone says Ada's childhood name. He dismisses it, but his hands shake. Emotional beat: dread of being seen after years of hiding.

chapters.title: The Smuggler Who Knew Too Much
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, a sharp-tongued smuggler and Ada's occasional ally. She reports that King Vessar's surveyors are charting every pass into Thornfell, asking about 'the sealed door.' Ada realizes his gate is no longer ignored. Emotional beat: the end of safety.

chapters.title: A Name in the Frost
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The god speaks again: it names Ada's sister Lira, sold to the court beneath the mountain seventy years ago to seal the gods' imprisonment. Ada, kept young by gate-warding magic, realizes he is the last witness. Emotional beat: grief reopened.

chapters.title: The Priestess Without a God
chapters.summary: Yara's POV introduction—a defrocked priestess of the old faith drinking herself numb in the free city of Corvale. She receives an impossible sign: her dead order's sigil burning on her palm. Emotional beat: reluctant hope.

chapters.title: Bargains at the Gate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Vessar's captain arrives demanding the gate's keys and records. Ada stalls, lies beautifully, and sends word to Sefa: he needs a crew for a descent no one returns from. Emotional beat: crossing the line from bystander to conspirator.

chapters.title: The Crew of Broken Things
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Assembling the team: Yara the fallen priestess, Dov a mute tunnel-digger exile, and Pell, a teenage pickpocket who worships Ada without knowing why. Each carries a debt or a wound. Emotional beat: the fragile first stitch of found family.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The company travels smugglers' roads only Ada knows, while the old gods whisper directions through stones and streams—the land itself wants them to succeed. First ambush by Vessar's outriders; they escape narrowly. Emotional beat: trust tested under fire.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Burn Their Candles
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Resupply in Corvale reveals the political stakes: free cities debating surrender while Vessar's armies mass. Pell witnesses a mob turn on an old-god shrine and sees Yara defend it. Emotional beat: understanding what they're really fighting for.

chapters.title: Under the Thorn
chapters.summary: Dov's POV (told in near-wordless interiority). The descent begins through Dov's ancestral tunnels, marked with carvings of the bargain: seven souls for seven locks. Six are listed. The seventh name is scraped away. Emotional beat: claustrophobic awe and mounting horror.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They reach the subterranean court of the buried gods—beautiful, wrong, lit by memories. Souls drift there like lanterns. Ada sees one wearing his sister's face, unchanged at seventeen. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Terms of the Old Bargain
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Negotiating with the Court's steward, a creature of contracts. Souls can be redeemed—but only by an equivalent freely given, and Vessar's envoy is already there offering an army's worth of souls for the seventh lock's power. Emotional beat: the price of justice outside any law.

chapters.title: What Vessar Bought
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Captured correspondence reveals Vessar's plan: he doesn't want to free the gods, he wants to wear the seventh lock as a crown and rule both worlds. Above, his vanguard crosses the pass Ada left unguarded. Emotional beat: guilt and fury.

chapters.title: Lira
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada reaches his sister's soul-lantern. She remembers nothing but the gate, and asks if mother still waits there. He cannot lie to her twice. He tells her everything, and she chooses to hear it. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The steward names the exchange: a soul freely given for a soul taken back. Ada offers his own. The others refuse to let him—Sefa counters with the smugglers' ancient debt to the mountain, Dov offers his clan's name, Pell simply says 'not him.' Emotional beat: found family refusing to spend its own.

chapters.title: Vessar at the Gate
chapters.summary: Interleaved POVs. Vessar's army reaches Hollowgate; the gate-warding fails because Ada abandoned his post. Refugees flood through ahead of the soldiers. The seventh lock begins to crack. Emotional beat: consequences arriving all at once.

chapters.title: The Stolen Crown
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Vessar descends with his envoy and seizes the seventh lock, beginning the rite to bind the old gods as weapons. The Court turns on everyone. Chaos: souls scattering, tunnels collapsing, Dov holding a passage open at terrible cost. Emotional beat: everything breaking.

chapters.title: Seven Names Spoken
chapters.summary: Climax, Ada's POV. Yara performs the rite her order was made for; Sefa and Pell fight their way to the lock; Ada speaks all seven names—including his sister's and, finally, his own, offering his long unnatural life as the freely given price. The lock shatters; the gods wake whole, and take Vessar's stolen crown apart thread by thread. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice answered by grace.

chapters.title: What the Gods Decided
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The wakened gods judge: they return Ada's years, keep Lira's soul in the living world reborn as a young woman with new memories, and bind themselves to answer prayers at gates and crossroads forever. Vessar is given to the mountain's mercy, which is colder than execution. Emotional beat: justice that law could never deliver.

chapters.title: The Gate Reopened
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada returns to Hollowgate—not as a keeper of secrets but as a keeper of passage. No more bribes, no more ledgers of small sins: the gate stands open to refugees fleeing the war's aftermath, provisioned by the free cities' new covenant with the gods. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Lira, newly alive, arrives at the gate with no memory of Ada but an inexplicable feeling of home. Pell introduces them; Ada lets the relationship begin fresh rather than claiming what was lost. Sefa and Dov settle nearby. Emotional beat: joy that doesn't erase grief but shares a table with it.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered at Hollowgate
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, closing frame mirroring chapter one. A traveler prays at the gatepost; frost blooms; the old gods answer gently. Ada logs no sins tonight—only names, offered freely, of everyone who has a place here. Final line: the gate stays open. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted.
